classification.difficultyReason: Use the total heads and feet to distinguish two kinds of animals.

content.prompt: A family had a collection of animals. When the council asked them how many birds and how many beasts they had, they answered, ‘Well, we have 36 heads and 100 feet in total.’ How many birds and how many beasts did the family have?

answer.short:
22 birds and 14 beasts.

Start with two feet per animal; each four-footed beast accounts for two extra feet.
answer.worked:
If all 36 animals had two feet, there would be $36\times2=72$ feet. Each four-footed beast adds two feet to this total.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Extra feet}&=100-72\\\text{Extra feet}&=28\\\text{Beasts}&=28\div2\\\text{Beasts}&=14\\\text{Birds}&=36-14\\\text{Birds}&=22\end{align*}$$

Check: $22\times2+14\times4=100$ feet.
